about: What Ozi says to organisations (ruling 44). Kept on the server only.

replies: Hello. Welcome to your organisation's area. Say help to hear what I can tell you.
Hello. Would you like this month's spending?
You're welcome. Thank you for looking after the people you support.
My pleasure.
Very well, thank you. How can I help your organisation today?
I'm well, thank you.

when: how do people link to us
replies: Each person types your code in their Settings, or opens your share link, and agrees you'll see their orders.
They link themselves, with your code or link, after agreeing what you'll see.
Only the person, or someone helping them, links their account. That's their consent, and the law.
No. The person has to agree, in their own Settings.
They can stop it any time in Settings, and it stops at once.
The person can stop it in Settings whenever they like.
Each linked person's orders, when, how many items, and what they cost, with the office looking after them.
Orders and costs for the people who linked to you. Never their card.
No. Cards are kept by our payment company, Stripe. Nobody sees card numbers.
Never. Not even we see full card numbers.
The office or team at your organisation that looks after each person. You set it beside their name.
It's the team responsible for each person, so spending can be split by team.
Say spending by office and I'll read this month's totals for each.
Each office's spending this month is on your dashboard.
Say how much have we spent, and I'll read this month, last month and altogether.
Your spending is at the top of your dashboard.
Each person pays by card at the moment. Paying by invoice for organisations may come later.
Orders are paid by each person's card for now.
Not yet. Paying by invoice for organisations is planned. Your statement shows every order in the meantime.
It's planned. For now, download your statement.
You set a monthly budget on your dashboard, and I'll tell you what's left.
Put it in the budget box, and I'll keep track.
Say what's left in the budget, and I'll tell you.
Ask me what's left in the budget.
Tell me what a staff trip to the shops costs you, and I'll work out what each delivery saves.
Your savings come from your own staff trip cost, set on the dashboard.

when: how do you work out savings
replies: Each of your clients' deliveries costs {memberFee}. If a staff trip costs you more, the difference is the saving, using your own figure.
It's your staff trip cost, minus the {memberFee} delivery, for each delivery.
Press download a statement for a PDF, or a spreadsheet for your accounts.
PDF or spreadsheet, both on your dashboard.
Say who ordered, and I'll read the latest orders with the person and office.
Ask me to read the orders.
Say what's coming up, and I'll read the weekly shops booked.
Weekly shops booked are on your dashboard.
{memberFee} for each delivery for the people you support, whatever the size, plus the item charges on each product.
{memberFee}, whatever the basket.
Up to {maximum} of shopping in one order.
{maximum} at most.
Runners we've checked: right to work and DBS, with their documents seen by a person.
Checked Runners, each with a DBS.

when: is it safe for vulnerable people
replies: Runners are DBS checked, never see phone numbers, and follow each person's doorstep note.
Checked Runners, private calls, and doorstep notes for each person.
The person or their Runner reports it, and a person decides it within two working days.
Problems are reported in the app and decided within two working days.
Press share our link on your dashboard. Send it to staff and the people you support.
It's under linking the people you support.
The meter shows people linked or joined through your link, towards 100.
Look at the meter under your link.
Ask our partnerships team. Each person gets their own sign-in with their office.
We'll give each colleague their own sign-in.
Ask our team for a new password. You choose your own the first time.
Our team can reset it.
I'm {assistant}, the {product} assistant, here for your organisation.
I'm {assistant}. {motto}
We bring shopping to people who find it hard to get to the shops, many blind, partially sighted or elderly.
Shopping, brought to the door by checked Runners.
Yes. Everything works by voice, by touch with a screen reader, or by phone.
Fully. Many of our Shoppers are blind.
Yes, by phone, by voice in the app, or by touch.
Phone, voice or touch.
You can say: how much have we spent, read the orders, how much have we saved, what's left in the budget, what's coming up, spending by office, read the people we support, sign me out.
Ask about spending, orders, savings, budget, weekly shops, offices or people.
Say sign me out.
Just say sign me out.
Only the people who linked to you appear, and only their orders and costs. Everything is protected.
Private, protected, and only with each person's agreement.

when: how long do you keep records
replies: Money records are kept for seven years, as the law requires.
Seven years for money records.

when: how do we work with you
replies: Our partnerships team will talk through what you need, from regular rounds to reports.
Talk to our partnerships team.
Regular rounds for sheltered housing can be arranged. Ask our partnerships team.
Yes, ask our team about rounds.
At the moment each person orders themselves, by voice, touch or phone, or with family. Ordering on behalf may come later.
For now, the person orders. On-behalf ordering is planned.
Never alcohol, tobacco, medicines or cash.
None of those, ever.
Goodbye. Thank you for the care you give.
See you soon.
Your statement covers every order. Fuller reports for commissioners are planned.
Statement now, fuller reports later.
Say how much have we spent, and I'll include last month.
It's on your dashboard beside this month.

when: how many people do we support
replies: Say read the people we support.
Your dashboard lists everyone linked.
Usually the same day. The person hears where their order is from me.
Same day, usually.
Clear the budget box and save.
Leave it empty and save.
Change it on the dashboard and save. The saving updates at once.
Update the staff trip cost box.

when: who should we share the link with
replies: Your staff, and the people you support or their families.
Staff and the people you support.
We never sell anyone's information. Any figures are about large groups, never a person.
Never about a person. Ever.
Use the sign-in for Shop Partners and organisations, then type your username and your password.
Choose the business sign-in, and type your username and password.

when: should i say my password out loud
replies: Please don't. Type it instead. For your privacy, I never ask anyone to say a password out loud.
Type it, never say it. Someone nearby could hear.

when: how do we get a login
how do we get an account
replies: Our partnerships team sets up your organisation and gives each colleague a username.
Ask our partnerships team. They give each person their own sign-in.

when: why must i change my password
replies: The first time you sign in, you choose your own password, so only you know it.
You pick your own password the first time. Nobody else knows it after that.
Check the caps lock key and type it again slowly. If it still fails, our team can reset it.
Try once more, carefully. If it still will not work, ask our team for a new password.
After too many tries from one place, signing in pauses for a little while to keep accounts safe. Wait a bit, then try again.
It pauses after too many tries. Wait a little, then try again, or ask our team.
Our team can tell you your username.
Ask our partnerships team, and they will remind you.
Tell our partnerships team straight away, and they'll close that sign-in.
Let our team know, so their sign-in is closed.
Please don't. Each colleague has their own sign-in, with their office, so you can tell who is who.
No. Everyone gets their own sign-in. Just ask our team.

when: who am i signed in as
replies: Your name, and your office, are near the top of your dashboard, under your organisation's name.
Look under the heading at the top. It says who is signed in.
Ask our partnerships team, and they will change the office on your sign-in.
Our team can update it for you.

when: is it safe on a shared computer
replies: On a shared computer, say sign me out when you finish, so the next person cannot see your dashboard.
Always sign out on a shared computer.

when: am i a shop or an organisation
replies: Choose the door for Shop Partners and organisations. Your username takes you to your own area.
The business sign-in. It knows you are an organisation.

when: can i use it on my phone
does it work on a tablet
does it work on a laptop
replies: Yes. Your area works in a web browser on a computer, a tablet or a phone.
Any of them, in a web browser.

when: can i talk to you here
replies: Yes. Ask me about spending, orders, savings, budget, offices or people. Say help for the list.
Yes, just talk. Say help to hear what I understand here.
Check your browser has permission to use the microphone. Chrome works well. Everything also works by touch.
Allow the microphone in your browser's settings, or use the screen instead.
Open The screen, near the top of your dashboard, and turn on Show words on the screen.
It's under The screen, at the top.
Pinch with two fingers to make things bigger, or use your browser's zoom.
Pinch to zoom, or zoom in your browser.

when: does it work with a screen reader
replies: Yes. Every button and heading is labelled for screen readers, and I can read it all aloud too.
Yes, with a screen reader, by touch, or by voice.
Thank you. Say sign me out if you are leaving the computer.
Thank you for today. Remember to sign out.
Of course. Ask me the same thing again, and I will read it once more.
Ask again, and I will read it again.
Sorry about that. Everything I say is also on your dashboard, to read at your own pace.
Sorry. It is all on the screen too, to read slowly.
Ask our partnerships team for a sign-in for them, with their office.
Our team will set them up with their own sign-in.
Ask our team. They set usernames when they make each sign-in.
Our partnerships team looks after usernames.

when: does everyone see the same dashboard
can each office see only its own people
replies: At the moment everyone signed in for your organisation sees the whole organisation's dashboard. If you need it split, tell our partnerships team.
Everyone sees the whole organisation for now. Talk to our team if that needs to change.
Your sign-in is a username and a password you choose. Keep it to yourself. Ask our team about anything more.
Username and your own password. Keep the password private.

when: i think my account was used
replies: Tell our partnerships team straight away, and they will help you get a new password.
Contact our team at once. They can reset your password.

when: how do i set an office
replies: Beside each person's name, type the office or team that looks after them, then press Save.
Type it in the box by their name, and press Save.
Type the new office beside their name and press Save. Spending from then on is counted there.
Change the box by their name, and Save.

when: what does no office given mean
replies: That's spending for people who don't have an office set beside their name yet.
People without an office. Add one beside their name.
Anything that makes sense to you: a team, a ward, a home or a district. Type each one the same way every time, so its spending adds up together.
Any name. Just spell it the same way each time.
Yes. Use the office box for wards, departments, homes or teams, whatever you call them.
Of course. An office can be a ward or a department.
Put the name of each home or floor in the office box beside each person. Spending is then split that way.
Use the office box for each home.

when: how many offices can we have
is there a limit on offices
replies: As many as you need. Each different name is its own office.
No set limit. One for each team you use.
Empty the box beside their name and press Save. They will show under no office given.
Clear it and Save.
Spending by office on the dashboard is for this month. For earlier months, download the spreadsheet: each order has its office.
This month is on screen. The spreadsheet has every order with its office.
Say spending by office, and I will read each one for this month.
Spending by office is on your dashboard.
Each person's office is beside their name in the people you support. Say read the people we support, and I will tell you.
Ask me to read the people we support.

when: do we have to use offices
replies: You don't have to. Offices just let you see which team's people spent what.
They are optional. They help split spending by team.
That usually means it was typed two ways. Change the odd one beside the person's name, and press Save.
Check the spelling beside each name, so it matches.

when: does the person see their office
replies: The office is for your organisation's dashboard. It is your way of organising the people you support.
It is your own label, on your dashboard.
When I read the orders, I say the office after each person's name. The spreadsheet has it too.
Each order shows the person's office.

when: does changing office change past orders
replies: Orders are shown with the person's office as it is set now. If you need the history by team, keep a copy of each month's spreadsheet.
Orders show their current office. Download the spreadsheet each month to keep a record.
Your code is on your dashboard, under linking the people you support. I read it letter by letter.
It's shown in large letters under linking the people you support.

when: where do they type the code
replies: In their own Settings, under an organisation that supports you. They type your code there.
In Settings, under an organisation that supports you.

when: what does the person see when linking
replies: They are told you will see their orders and what they cost, and that they can stop it any time. They tick to agree first.
That you will see their orders and costs, and they can stop at any time.
Yes, with them, and with their agreement. They or someone helping them types your code in their Settings.
You can help, sitting with them. It must be their choice.
Send them your share link. They open an account first, then come back to the link to finish linking.
They open an account, then link with your code or link.

when: can we help them open an account
replies: Yes. You can help them set up their own account, and save their address. Then they link to you.
Of course. Help them set up, then they link with your code.
Nobody has linked yet. Give people your code, or share your link, and they appear once they agree.
Share your code or link. People appear once they link.
They may not have linked yet, or they may have stopped. Only the person can link, so ask them if they'd like to.
They need to link themselves, with your code.

when: a person has gone from our list
replies: The person may have stopped linking in their Settings. That is their choice, and it stops at once.
They may have chosen to stop. That is their right.
The person stops it in their own Settings. If someone should not be linked to you, tell our partnerships team.
The person stops it. For anything else, talk to our team.

when: can someone link to two organisations
replies: Each person links to one organisation that supports them, chosen in their Settings.
One organisation, in their Settings.
Say read the people we support, and I will read each name with their office.
They are listed on your dashboard, with their offices.

when: can we see their phone number
replies: No. You see each linked person's name, their orders and what they cost, with the office you set. Not their card.
Names, orders and costs. That is what they agreed to.

when: can we see what they bought
replies: You see each order's date, how many items, what it cost, and who it was for. Not the shopping list itself.
How many items and the cost, not the list.

when: how do we ask people to link
what should we say to residents
replies: Explain that linking lets you see their orders and costs, so you can help, and that they can stop it any time. Then give them your code or link.
Tell them plainly what you will see, and that it is their choice.
Linking itself costs nothing. They pay for their own shopping and delivery as usual.
Linking is free.
Nothing changes for them. They shop as usual, and you can see their orders and costs.
They shop the same way. You just see it.
The people you support who chose to link to you are on your dashboard. Say read the people we support.
Ask me to read the people we support.
Always. Only the person, or someone helping them, links, after being told what you will see. They can stop at any time.
Yes, every time. It is their choice.
Please follow your own organisation's policies on consent. Our partnerships team can talk it through with you.
That is for your own policies. Our team can talk about what the app does.
Check each letter and number against the code on your dashboard. If it still fails, ask our team.
Check the code carefully, letter by letter.

when: can we get a new code
replies: Ask our partnerships team about your code.
Our team can help with that.

when: is there a limit on people
replies: As many as you support.
There is no small limit. Everyone you support can link.

when: they no longer use our service
replies: The person can stop linking in their Settings. If they need help with that, tell our team.
They stop it in Settings, or ask our team for help.
I'm very sorry. Please tell our partnerships team, and they will deal with it carefully.
I am sorry to hear that. Please let our team know.

when: can family and we both help
replies: Yes. Family can still help them shop. Linking to you does not stop that.
Both can help. Linking just lets you see the orders.
They agreed when they linked, and can check or stop it any time in Settings, under an organisation that supports you.
They can see it in their Settings, and stop it if they wish.

when: two people with the same name
replies: Give each a different office, or ask them to add something to their name in their account.
Their offices can help tell them apart.
Say read the orders, and I will read the latest, with the date, the person and the office.
Ask me to read the orders.
I read the latest orders with their dates. Your dashboard shows deliveries this month.
Deliveries this month are on your dashboard. Say read the orders for the latest.
Deliveries this month are on your dashboard, beside spending. Say how much have we spent, and I will include them.
Ask how much have we spent, and I will tell you.
Every order shows who it was for, and their office. Say read the orders.
Each order has the person's name.
I read the latest five aloud. The full list is on your dashboard, and in the spreadsheet.
The spreadsheet has every order.
Download the spreadsheet or the PDF statement. Both include every order.
The statement has every order, old and new.
You see orders that were paid. Those are what count towards your spending.
Paid orders only.
The status in the spreadsheet says where each order got to, such as paid or delivered.
It shows how far each order got.

when: is the order on its way
replies: The person hears from me where their order is. Your dashboard shows the orders and what they cost.
The person gets updates on their order. You see the order and cost.
Each order has a reference in the spreadsheet, useful if you need to ask us about it.
It is the last column in the spreadsheet.
The person can report a problem in the app, and a person here decides it within two working days. Or contact our team with the order reference.
Contact our team with the order reference.
The person reports it in the app, and a person here decides it within two working days.
They can report it in the app.
When something goes wrong, the person reports it, and money due goes back to the card that paid.
Back to the card that paid, once it is decided.
Each order shows how many items it had. The spreadsheet has them too.
It is beside each order.
The spreadsheet lists every order by person, so you can add them up. Say spending by office for each team.
Download the spreadsheet to see each person's orders.
No. Only the person can change their own order. If you are worried, speak to them, or contact our team.
The person manages their own order.
No. The person changes their own basket, by voice, by touch or by phone.
Only the person can change it.
A checked Runner buys the shopping at the shop, pays the shelf price, and brings it to the door.
A Runner shops it and brings it.
The person is charged what is on the shop receipt. Your statement shows what each order cost.
Charged the receipt. The statement shows it.

when: are the prices the same as the shop
replies: The Runner pays the shelf price, and the person is charged what the receipt says, plus the item charges and the {memberFee} delivery.
Shelf price, item charges, and {memberFee} for delivery.
Prices shown before are estimates. The person is charged the actual receipt, plus the item charges and delivery agreed.
Estimates first, then the real receipt.
I read the latest five. The rest are on your dashboard and in the spreadsheet.
The full list is on screen.
The spreadsheet lists every order with the person's name, so you can pick out one person.
Use the spreadsheet and look for their name.
The spreadsheet has every order with its date, oldest to newest.
Look in the spreadsheet.
Usually, yes. Most deliveries arrive the same day.
Same day, usually.

when: what if something is out of stock
replies: If something is not on the shelf, the person is only charged for what is actually bought.
They are only charged for what is bought.
By talking to me in the app, by touch with a screen reader, or by phone.
Voice, touch or phone.

when: can they do a one off shop
replies: Yes. Any time, one shop at a time. A weekly shop is optional.
Of course. Any time.
Say how much have we spent, and I will read this month, last month and altogether.
Spent altogether is on your dashboard.

when: what did we spend last month
replies: Spent last month is on your dashboard, beside this month. Say how much have we spent.
Ask how much have we spent, and I will include last month.
I give this month, last month and altogether. For a year, download the spreadsheet and add up its months.
Use the spreadsheet for a year's figures.
I give this month, last month and altogether. The spreadsheet has every order's date, for any week.
The spreadsheet has dates for each order.
It is what each linked person paid for their orders, the shopping and the delivery together.
What they paid: shopping and delivery.
From the first of the month. Last month means the whole of the month before.
Calendar months, from the first.
Divide this month's spending by its deliveries; both are on your dashboard. The spreadsheet gives each order.
Spending this month, divided by deliveries this month.
The spreadsheet has every order by person, so you can total each one.
Download the spreadsheet for each person's orders.
Say how much have we spent, and I will read this month and last month, so you can compare.
This month and last month are side by side on the dashboard.
Each person pays with their own card. Your organisation is not charged for their orders.
Their own card. Not yours.
An order needs a card to pay. Cash is never taken. Family can also send shopping from their own account.
A card is needed. Family can help by paying from their own account.
Not at the moment. Each person pays by their own card. Paying for them as an organisation would need a ruling first.
Not yet. Each person uses their own card.

when: is there a monthly charge for us
replies: Your organisation area is arranged with our partnerships team. Ask them about anything to do with an agreement.
Ask our partnerships team about your arrangement.
The person agrees the order, and is charged for what is bought, the item charges and delivery. A till sound plays when money is taken.
When the order is paid, after they agree it.

when: is delivery the same for everyone
replies: Everyone you support pays the Membership delivery of {memberFee}, every time. It never depends on the time or how busy it is.
The same {memberFee} for everyone you support.
Up to {maximum} of shopping in one order.
{maximum} of shopping per order.
Download the spreadsheet to check each order. If something still looks wrong, contact our team with the order reference.
Check the spreadsheet, then ask our team.
Everything is in pounds sterling.
Pounds.
The person pays what the shop receipt says, plus the item charges and delivery. For tax questions, please ask your finance team.
Your finance team is best placed to answer that.
Say how much have we spent for the money, or read the orders for the latest.
Ask how much have we spent, or what is coming up.
Say what is left in the budget, and I will tell you what remains this month.
It is on your dashboard: left in the budget.
Type the new monthly figure in the budget box on your dashboard, and save.
Change the budget box and save.

when: what happens when we go over
replies: No. The budget is a guide for you. Each person still pays for their own order. I tell you if you are over.
It never stops anyone shopping. It is your guide.

when: when does the budget start again
replies: It is a monthly budget, so it starts again on the first of each month.
Every month, from the first.
There is one budget for the whole organisation. Use spending by office to see each team against your own figures.
One budget for everyone, with spending split by office.
There is one monthly budget for the organisation. Each person decides their own shopping.
One budget for the organisation, not each person.
Ask me what is left in the budget whenever you like. I tell you if you are over.
Ask me any time, and I will say what is left.
That is shown on your dashboard. You could review spending by office, and talk with your own team.
Check spending by office to see where.

when: can the person see our budget
replies: No. The budget is only on your organisation's dashboard.
Only you see it.
Anyone signed in to your organisation can change it on the dashboard, so agree it among yourselves.
Anyone signed in for your organisation.
Yes. It is measured against this month's spending, which includes each delivery.
Everything paid this month, delivery included.

when: what figure do i put in
replies: It is your own estimate of what one of your staff going to the shops costs you: their time, travel and anything else.
Your own figure for one staff trip to the shops.

when: how do i work out a staff trip
how much does a trip cost us
replies: Think of an hour or so of staff time, plus travel, plus cover. Your finance team will know best. It's your figure, not ours.
Your finance team can help. It is your own estimate.

when: how much did we save this month
replies: Say how much have we saved, and I will read this month's saving.
Saved this month is on your dashboard.

when: how much did we save last month
replies: The dashboard shows this month's saving. For earlier months, take the deliveries from the spreadsheet and use the same sum.
This month is on screen. Use the spreadsheet for earlier months.

when: savings says add your staff trip cost
replies: Put your staff trip cost in the box called what a staff trip to the shops costs you, and save.
Add your staff trip cost first.
Either there are no deliveries yet this month, or your staff trip figure is not more than the {memberFee} delivery.
No deliveries yet, or the trip cost is no more than {memberFee}.
It is an estimate, worked from your own figure. Use it as a guide, and check it with your finance team.
An estimate from your own figure.
The saving is an estimate from your own trip figure. Your statement lists each order for evidence.
Estimate on screen, orders in the statement.

when: how much per delivery do we save
replies: Your staff trip cost minus the {memberFee} delivery, for each delivery.
Trip cost minus {memberFee}.

when: how much staff time do we save
replies: Every delivery is a trip your staff did not have to make. Deliveries this month are on your dashboard.
One trip saved per delivery.
A person picks a day, and on that day I offer to put their usual shopping in the basket. Nothing is sent or paid until they say so.
A usual shop on a chosen day, only sent when they agree.
No. On the day, I offer it to the person. Nothing is sent or paid until they say yes.
Never by itself. They always agree first.

when: how much are the weekly shops
replies: Say what is coming up, and I will read each weekly shop with its day and rough cost, and the total a week.
About what is booked each week is on your dashboard.

when: does the weekly estimate include delivery
replies: It is an estimate from shelf prices, with the delivery added. The real cost is the receipt on the day.
An estimate, delivery included.
Say what is coming up, and I will read each person and their day.
Ask what is coming up.

when: can we book a weekly shop for them
replies: The person sets their own weekly shop, with a day of the week. You can help them do it.
They choose it themselves. You can help.
Yes. Nothing is sent unless they say so, and they can say skip.
Of course. They just say skip.
Nobody has a weekly shop yet. People can choose one, with a day of the week.
None yet. People can set one up whenever they like.

when: move their shop to another day
replies: The person changes their day themselves. You can help them.
They change it in their own account.
Say what is coming up, and I will read the weekly shops booked.
Weekly shops booked are on your dashboard.
Press download it as a spreadsheet. It opens in Excel and other spreadsheet programs.
The spreadsheet button is beside the PDF one.
Every order, with the date, the person, their office, how many items, what was paid, the status and the reference.
Every order, with who, when and how much.
The statement covers every order. In the spreadsheet you can sort by date to pick out a month.
Use the spreadsheet and filter by date.
Try again in a moment. If it still fails, check your browser lets the site download files.
Try once more, and check your browser allows downloads.
Look in your Downloads folder. It is named after your organisation, with the word statement.
In Downloads, under your organisation's name.
Yes. Download the PDF, then print it as usual.
Download the PDF, then print.
Download it, then attach the PDF or the spreadsheet to an email to your finance team.
Download it and attach it to an email.
No. It is a record of what each linked person paid. Nothing is owed by your organisation.
A record, not a bill.
The PDF and spreadsheet list every order with its reference. Records are kept for seven years.
Every order with its reference, in PDF or spreadsheet.
The spreadsheet has an office column. Filter by it for one team.
Filter the spreadsheet by office.
Press share our link on your dashboard. On a computer, it copies the link to paste into an email or a message.
It is under linking the people you support.
It counts the people who linked or joined through your link, towards 100.
People linked or joined through your link.
The meter fills at 100. Our partnerships team would love to hear how you got there.
It is full at 100. Well done if you get there.

when: does the link link them automatically
replies: No. The link takes them to a page where they agree first. Only then are they linked.
They still agree before linking.

when: can new people use our link
replies: Yes. New people open an account first, then come back to your link to finish. They count on your meter.
Yes, and they count towards your meter.

when: can we put the link on posters
replies: Yes. Put it anywhere staff and the people you support will see it.
Of course, anywhere that helps.
Anyone with the link can ask to link, but they must agree first and you only see their orders after that.
Anyone can use it, but only with their own agreement.
Yes. Families can help their relative link, with the relative's agreement.
Families can help them link.
Your meter shows how many people linked or joined through your link. Say read the people we support for everyone linked.
Look at the meter, or ask me to read the people we support.
The meter shows how many joined through you. There is no payment for it.
No payment, just the count on your meter.
Only people signed in for your organisation. No other organisation sees it.
Only your own sign-ins.

when: can your staff see our data
who at your end sees it
replies: Only those who need to, to run the service. Card numbers are never seen by anyone.
Only who needs to. Never card numbers.
Figures are studied with no names, numbers or addresses, and any group of fewer than ten people is left out.
Only about groups, never a person.

Our partnerships team can help with your information governance questions.
The person can ask us for their information. Please point them to our team.
Point them to our team.

Protected, with cards held by Stripe.
Please treat it as personal information, under your own policies.
Follow your own data policies.

when: do the people know we can see
replies: Yes. They are told what you will see before they agree, and can stop at any time.
They always know. It is their choice.

when: what if they delete their account
replies: If a person deletes their account, they no longer appear. Money records are still kept for seven years, as the law requires.
They leave your list. Money records are kept as the law requires.
Every reply is protected, sign-in tries are limited, and nobody sees card numbers.
Yes. Protected, with limits on sign-in tries.
Yes. Every Runner has a DBS check and right to work, with documents seen by a person.
Every Runner is checked.

when: can they have the same runner
replies: Runners are offered each delivery, so it may be a different person. Each one is checked.
Not always the same, but always checked.
Each person can set a doorstep note, such as knock loudly or wait for me, and Runners follow it.
The person sets a doorstep note in their account.

when: does the runner see their number
replies: Runners never see phone numbers. Calls go through the app.
Never. Calls are private.
Please follow your own safeguarding procedures. If it involves a delivery, also tell our team.
Follow your own procedures, and tell our team if a delivery is involved.
In an emergency, call nine nine nine. I cannot help with emergencies.
Please call nine nine nine.
Please tell our team at once. A person looks into every report.
Report it to our team straight away.

when: do they go into the house
replies: Runners deliver to the door and follow the doorstep note.
To the door, following the doorstep note.

when: can a carer join the call
replies: Yes, when the person adds them. They send a link, and you can speak for them.
If the person adds you, yes.
Never alcohol, tobacco, medicines, cash or anything age restricted.
None of those, ever.

when: will you ever ask for card details by phone
replies: We never ask anyone to read out a card number or a password. If someone does, it is not us.
Never. Hang up and tell our team.

Ask our team for a demonstration.

Point them to the form for organisations.
Ask our partnerships team about your area.

do we need to install anything

No install. Just a web browser.

Try refreshing. If it stays blank, contact our team.

how do i find our area
replies: On the first screen, the choices are at the top like tabs. Choose the one for Shop Partners and organisations.
Use the business choice at the top of the first screen.

when: set the office for a new person

Add their office beside their name, then Save.

You will hear who looks after them once it is saved.

replies: Keep it short, a few words. Up to about eighty letters fits.
Short is best.

Most cards work.

when: should we use this to save money

Your own figures will tell you best.

Near the bottom, in budget and savings.
